blogs.title: Getting Started with Flutter Development
blogs.author: Jafor Sadak
blogs.excerpt: A beginner-friendly guide to building your first cross-platform mobile app with Flutter and Dart by Jafor Sadak.
blogs.content:
Flutter is one of the most popular frameworks for building cross-platform mobile applications. In this article, I'll walk through how I started learning Flutter and built my first app.

Why Flutter? Flutter lets you write one codebase and deploy to both Android and iOS. The hot reload feature makes development fast and enjoyable.

Setting up your environment: Install the Flutter SDK, set up Android Studio or VS Code with the Flutter extension, and run flutter doctor to verify everything works.

Building your first app: Start with a simple counter app, then move to layouts, navigation, and state management. My myflutter-app project on GitHub is a good reference.

Jafor Sadak — software developer from Bangladesh, passionate about mobile development and open source.

blogs.author: Jafor Sadak
blogs.excerpt: Jafor Sadak shares his path from learning to code in 2022 to building 16+ GitHub repositories in C++, Java, Python, and Flutter.
blogs.content:
My name is Jafor Sadak, and I'm a computer science student and software developer from Bangladesh. I started coding in 2022 and haven't looked back since.

Early days: I began with C and Java in university courses. Compiler design and data structures challenged me but taught me how computers really work under the hood.

Projects that shaped me: From an OpenGL village renderer to a Java Swing inventory system, each project taught me something new. I publish everything on GitHub at github.com/jaforsadakdiu.

What's next: I'm focused on full-stack development, mobile apps with Flutter, and contributing to open source. If you're searching for Jafor Sadak or jaforsadak online — welcome to my official portfolio.

Feel free to reach out for collaborations, internships, or just to say hello.

blogs.title: Understanding Compiler Design Basics
blogs.author: Jafor Sadak
blogs.excerpt: An overview of lexical analysis, parsing, and code generation from Jafor Sadak's compiler design university project.
blogs.content:
Compiler design is a fundamental topic in computer science. It teaches you how programming languages are translated into machine code.

Lexical analysis: The first phase breaks source code into tokens — keywords, identifiers, operators, and literals.

Syntax analysis: Parsing builds a tree structure from tokens according to grammar rules. This is where you catch syntax errors.

Code generation: The final phase produces target code, whether assembly or bytecode.

My compiler-design-project on GitHub implements these phases in C. It's a great learning exercise for anyone studying systems programming.

Written by Jafor Sadak — follow my work at jaforsadak.dev.
